facts.claim: Santorini Gem's home page is headed 'Your Wedding in Santorini Gem' and says 'The majestic caldera views will make a perfect backdrop to your very special moment, while Santorini Gem Wedding Venue and Villa will enchant your guests.' It describes a private estate 'with the flawless views and the wonderful green spaces for the celebration of your marriage'.

Santorini Gem's home page says the venue 'is able to host large or smaller-scale events, with outdoor and indoor spaces, selected services and a variety of menus', offers wedding planning services, and frames 'an emotional ceremony to unfold at sunset'. Its ceremony and reception teaser reads 'Exchange vows in the Caldera among friends and family. Celebrate your special day with a dinner party!'

Santorini Gem's venue page lists 'An incredible ceremony venue facing the volcanos, a dining area and a cosy bar, a large pool overlooking the famous Caldera with wonderful poolside areas and an imposing luxury wedding villa', and refers to 'the imposing caldera views'. No guest capacity figure appears on the pages read (a venue policy PDF and rental brochure are linked but were not read).

Santorini Gem's villa page says 'Perched on the legendary caldera cliffs of Santorini, Gem Villa is a private sanctuary', with 'five elegant bedrooms accommodating up to eight guests', four bathrooms, two living rooms, a private pool facing the horizon and gardens.
Santorini Gem's contact block gives the address only as 'GEM, Santorini, Cyclades, Greece'; the pages read do not name the village or area.

Erosantorini's estate page describes an 'exclusive-use estate' with 'panoramic views of Santorini's iconic villages, dazzling sunsets, and the legendary caldera', five suites for up to ten guests on two acres, located 'on the edge of the caldera in the Messaria area, just 2 kilometers south of Santorini's bustling capital, Fira'. The home page lists a private chapel and an 'Events' heading but no wedding wording on the pages read, so it does not yet meet the inclusion rule.

Kivotos Santorini's home page says it is 'Built high atop the cliffside in Imerovigli, the most exclusive spot on the caldera' and the Signature Suite offers 'panoramic views of the island's breathtaking caldera'. No wedding wording appears on the home page, so it does not meet the inclusion rule on this read.

Cavo Tagoo Santorini's home page says it is 'Set between breathtaking Caldera views and an iconic infinity pool' and its concierge list includes 'SPECIAL OCCASION PLANNING'; the word wedding does not appear on the page read, so it does not meet the inclusion rule.

Perivolas (Oia) says it 'boasts a prime cliffside location overlooking the Caldera' (home) and 'with its stunning Caldera views' (contact page); neither page mentions weddings, so it does not meet the inclusion rule on this read.
Esperas (Oia) describes its Ombra Restaurant with 'spectacular views of the Caldera'; the home and hotel pages read do not mention weddings, so it does not meet the inclusion rule on this read.

Celestia Grand's home page says 'Gaze beyond the horizon, where the caldera's majesty meets refined elegance' and calls itself the 'Most easily accessible caldera hotel'; no wedding wording appears on the home page, so it does not meet the inclusion rule on this read.

insider_details.detail: Santorini Gem pairs the event spaces with a five-bedroom villa for up to eight, so the couple and closest family can stay where the wedding happens; everyone else needs rooms elsewhere.
Santorini Gem frames the ceremony at sunset facing the volcano; a sunset ceremony means the reception runs after dark, so lighting and guest travel back to hotels need planning.
